# Earth Gravity — the full-pipeline fixture book

One short book (7 chapters, about 2,400 words) written to hit every edge case in one run of the whole pipeline. It
exists in four formats with the same text: `earth-gravity.txt`, `earth-gravity.md` (plus `images/`),
`earth-gravity.fb2` and `earth-gravity.epub`. A real local model translates it in minutes. It is used by the
whole-book e2e tests and for manual runs of the real app. Real books are only used for partial runs.

**Do not edit these files by hand.** All of them, including `manifest.json` and the images, are generated by one
script from one source, the `PARTS`/`CHAPTERS` data in `scripts/make-fixtures.py`:

```bash
python3 scripts/make-fixtures.py                     # regenerate (deterministic: same bytes every run)
python3 scripts/validate-translated-book.py --self-test
```

The self-test fails if a committed file no longer matches what the generator writes.

## Files

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `earth-gravity.epub` | EPUB 3 with an EPUB 2 NCX. It has a separate cover page, a title page, a copyright page, an in-book contents page, 7 chapters and a notes page, each a separate spine document. `nav.xhtml` is outside the spine and holds a visible `toc` nav and a `hidden` landmarks nav. The metadata sets title, creator, `dc:language en`, description, `cover-image` and the EPUB 2 `<meta name="cover">`. The stylesheet has an `@font-face` that points at the embedded font. `mimetype` is the first entry and is STORED. Zip timestamps are fixed. |
| `earth-gravity.fb2` | FB2 2.x in UTF-8 with a `<stylesheet>`, `title-info` (genre, author with first name, last name and nickname, annotation, keywords, coverpage, `lang en`, `src-lang`), `document-info` and `publish-info`. It has a notes body and three base64 `<binary>` images. |
| `earth-gravity.md` | CommonMark + GFM tables, the two extensions the reader enables. It has frontmatter (`title`, `author`, `lang: en`, `description`), ATX headings, a fenced code block, a table, lists, a block quote and relative image paths (`images/…`). |
| `earth-gravity.txt` | UTF-8 with LF line endings. Paragraphs are separated by blank lines. There is no Markdown syntax. Some paragraphs are hard-wrapped, quotes are indented, and lists, tables and verse are kept one line per item, row or line inside a single paragraph. |
| `images/cover.png`, `images/diagram.png`, `images/earth.jpg` | Tiny images generated with the standard library. `earth.jpg` is a baseline grayscale JPEG. All three are embedded in the EPUB and the FB2, and the Markdown links to them. |
| `BookLoomTestFont-DUMMY.otf` (EPUB only) | **Not a usable font.** It is a 12-byte OpenType header with zero tables. Its only job is to check that the font's bytes survive the round trip. |
| `manifest.json` | Generated facts that tests and manual checks can assert. See below. |

## Edge cases and what each one exercises

Block ids are the EPUB/FB2 `id` attributes. Markdown and TXT blocks are matched by position against the same
inventory in `manifest.json`.

| Case | Where | Exercises |
|---|---|---|
| Title page, copyright, contents, notes | `tp-*`, `cr-*`, `toc-*`, `note-*` | Front and back matter as ordinary segments. The contents links point into the spine (EPUB) or to section ids (FB2). |
| Recurring names in several forms | Dr. Eleanor Vance / Vance / Nell, Tomas Reyes / Reyes, Harrow Vale (also hard-wrapped across a TXT line break), the Meridian Survey Institute / the Institute, the Amulet | Glossary scan (FR-GLOSS-01), name policy (FR-BRIEF-05), name dictionary (FR-ALGO-05), and a consistent rendering across the book (the validator's `names` check) |
| Capitalised common words at sentence starts | "Well,", "Don't", "Words", "Seal", "Shield". They also appear as one-word paragraphs in `ch7` | Glossary-scan filters: none of them should be proposed as a name |
| Terms and units | km, m/s², 9.81, 6.674×10⁻¹¹, N·m²/kg², mGal, 784.8 N | Numbers stay in prose and are not masked (D-7). Units are kept |
| Numbers-only and symbol-only paragraphs | `2`, `XIV`, `§`, `***` (scene break, set apart by `<empty-line/>` in FB2), `9.81`, `978-0-00-000000-2`, `100%`… | `VerbatimRule` SYMBOLS / ROMAN_NUMERAL / SINGLE_CHARACTER: kept as written without a model call |
| NBSP-only and ZWSP-only paragraphs | `ch7-p2`, `ch7-p6` | Invisible text (FR-DOC-01): no segment in EPUB/FB2. TXT/MD hold the character, and the pipeline keeps it as NO_TEXT |
| Image-only paragraph | `ch5-imgp1` | An atomic image token with no text |
| Same image three times with the alt "diagram" | `ch2-fig1`, `ch5-imgp1`, `ch5-fig1` | Repeated alt text reuses one translation (`DraftShortcuts`), FR-DOC-11 / DD-47 |
| Same head `<title>` in every XHTML document | all spine documents | Same auxiliary text repeated in every document (`DraftShortcuts`) |
| Inline markup | italic, bold, nested bold+italic (`ch5-p1`), links with href (`ch5-p3`), drop cap `<span class="dropcap">G</span>ravity` (`ch1-p1`, `<style name="dropcap">` in FB2), footnote refs with backlinks (`<sup>` inside `<a epub:type="noteref">` in EPUB; `type="note"` in FB2) | Paired placeholder masking and the placeholder gate (FR-DOC-04/05, ADR-0040). Drop-cap pair order |
| Code and formula spans, code blocks | `<code>` in `ch1-p3`, `ch1-p7`, `ch3-p1` and table cells; `<pre>` / fenced blocks `*-pre*` | DD-49: an inline code span is one atomic token. Block code is excluded from segmentation. A cell that holds only code is not translated |
| Foreign passages | Latin paragraph `ch4-p7` (`xml:lang="la"`); French inline runs in `ch4-p9`, `ch4-p10` (`<span lang="fr">` / `<style xml:lang="fr">`); plain text in MD/TXT | Foreign-passage policy, keep-as-is by default (FR-BRIEF-04, DD-26) |
| Dialogue and non-ASCII punctuation | “ ” ‘ ’ — … « » throughout `ch1`, `ch4`, `ch7` | Punctuation survives. Echo and refusal checks on short dialogue lines |
| Table | `ch3-t1` (5×3, with code cells), `ch5-t1` (cells that hold only a percentage are verbatim) | FR-DOC-08: tables. Each cell is a segment |
| Ordered and unordered lists | `ch1-l1`, `ch2-l1`, `ch2-l2`; the contents list | List items as segments. In FB2 they are paragraphs prefixed with `1.`/`•` (FB2 has no list markup) |
| Block quote and epigraph | `ch1-q1` (FB2 `<epigraph>`, EPUB `blockquote.epigraph`), `ch5-q1` (`<cite>`) | Quote structure |
| Poem | `ch7-poem1` (FB2 `<poem><stanza><v>`, EPUB `<p class="verse">`, MD hard breaks, TXT one stanza per paragraph) | FR-DOC-08: verse |
| Very long paragraph | `ch6-p2`: 965 words, about 1,469 estimated tokens for `en` (1,958 if the language is unknown), over the 1,200-token chunk budget | Oversized-segment split (FR-ALGO-03/12, `OversizedSplit`) |
| Same sentence three times | "Every object with mass attracts every other object with mass." in `ch1-p2`, `ch5-p2`, `ch7-p8` | Translation memory. Under FR-ALGO-06 an exact match is reused automatically only when its neighbours match too, so expect a memory hit or suggestion, not necessarily automatic reuse |
| Heading identical to a body paragraph | `ch2-h1` and `ch2-p4`: "Gravity keeps the oceans in place" | Memory and summary must not mix up a heading and a paragraph with the same text |
| Footnotes | 3 notes; FB2 notes body; EPUB `aside epub:type="footnote"` with backlinks; MD links `[1](#note-1)`; TXT `[1]` | FR-DOC-08: footnotes. Backlink pairs that hold only a symbol (↩) |
| Images, fonts and binaries | 3 images + 1 font | FR-DOC-02: binary entries are byte-identical after export |
| Metadata and ToC labels | EPUB title/creator/description, nav and NCX labels; FB2 book-title, author, annotation; MD frontmatter values | FR-DOC-11 / DD-47: auxiliary units behind "Also translate" |
| Declared language | `dc:language`, FB2 `<lang>`, MD `lang:` | FR-DOC-07: updated to the target language on export |

## What the readers do not support

These were left out or written differently, and the manifest reflects that:

- **Markdown footnotes** (`[^1]`): the reader enables only the tables and autolink extensions. Footnote references
  are written as ordinary links (`[1](#note-1)`), and the notes are an ordered list with `[↩](#ref-N)` backlinks.
- **Markdown strikethrough, task lists, alerts, `<details>`, Mermaid**: these are in the original
  `earth-gravity.md` but were not carried over. Strikethrough is not enabled in the reader, and inline HTML is
  outside this fixture's scope.
- **Foreign-language runs in Markdown and TXT**: neither format can declare a language, so the Latin and French text
  is plain prose there and the app's foreign-passage policy cannot see it.
- **FB2 lists and footnote backlinks**: FB2 has no list markup, and `<a>` cannot carry an `id` for a backlink
  target. Lists become prefixed paragraphs, and notes have no backlink.
- **TXT images and code blocks**: they are omitted. Figure captions are kept as paragraphs.
- **A real embedded font**: one cannot be generated with the standard library alone, so a clearly named dummy is
  used.

## manifest.json

The manifest is generated together with the books, so it always matches them.

- `formats.<fmt>.blocks[]`: the block inventory in reading order. Each entry has `id`, `kind`, `category`, `text`
  (visible text) and `inline` (logical markup counts: `i`, `b`, `a`, `dc`, `fn`, `code`, `f`). The category is one
  of:
  - `translatable`
  - `verbatim`: numbers, symbols, a Roman numeral or a single character, the same rule as the pipeline's
    `VerbatimRule`
  - `foreign`
  - `invisible`
  - `code`
  - `image`
- `formats.<fmt>.block_count`, `blocks_by_category`, `translatable_blocks`, `images`, `footnote_refs`, `aux` (the
  auxiliary texts).
- `names` (each name with its `forms`), `glossary_bait`, `terms`, `repeated_sentence`, `heading_equals_body`,
  `long_paragraph` (words, characters, estimated tokens, the budget), `verbatim_texts`, `foreign`,
  `invisible_blocks`, `footnotes`, `links`, `binary_files` (SHA-256 of each image and the font).

Translatable blocks per format: EPUB 121, FB2 121, MD 115 (frontmatter values and alt texts are counted as `aux`,
not blocks), TXT 85 (lists, tables and stanzas are one paragraph each). The EPUB adds 47 auxiliary texts: head
titles, alts, nav/NCX labels and metadata.

## Checking a translated export

```bash
python3 scripts/validate-translated-book.py epub \
    modules/app/src/test/resources/fixtures/earth-gravity/earth-gravity.epub ~/Desktop/earth-gravity.uk.epub --lang uk
```

The validator prints one line per check and a final `PASS`/`FAIL` that names the failing block ids.

**Structure checks:**

- The container is valid: zip, `mimetype` first and STORED, every XML document well-formed.
- The block ids and their order are unchanged.
- Each block has the same inline markup: tags, link targets, image sources, footnote refs.
- Code spans are unchanged.
- Verbatim, code-only and invisible blocks are unchanged.
- Lists, tables and verse keep their line structure (TXT/MD), and indentation is kept.
- Images and fonts are byte-identical.
- No `⟦gN⟧` placeholder is left.
- Foreign passages are unchanged. A change here is only a `WARN`, because the policy may be set to translate.

**Language checks:**

- Every translatable block contains letters in the target script (Cyrillic for `uk`).
- No run of 6 or more untranslated source words. A run of 4–5 words is a `WARN`.
- Each name form is rendered one way. The check compares 4-letter stems, so grammatical case is tolerated. It
  reports the renderings it found and the block ids where the chosen rendering is missing. A name replaced by a
  pronoun also appears there, so review those ids.
- The declared language is updated. For Markdown this is only a `WARN`.

The self-test checks the validator itself:

- An identity "translation" passes structure and fails language.
- A transliterated stand-in translation passes.
- Each of seven deliberate defects is caught by the check meant for it.
